name: Molecule Builder
author: Alexandria samples
subject: chemistry
_fidelity: SINGLE BONDS ONLY. The simulation models covalent single bonds and nothing else, so it cannot represent O2, CO2, N2 or anything with a double or triple bond. That limit is stated in every task parameter's job line because a sim that permits an impossible molecule teaches something false and the student has no way to know — see `Alexandria - Interactives`, fidelity is a safety property. An engine declares what it CANNOT model, or Alexandria will cheerfully generate a task it gets wrong.

build-target.job: Ask the student to build one specific named molecule from individual atoms.

formula.job: The molecular formula to build, written plainly, e.g. H2O, CH4, NH3, C2H6, CH4O. Only H, C, N and O are available, and the builder models SINGLE BONDS ONLY — never ask for a molecule that needs a double or triple bond, so no O2, no CO2, no N2, no CH2O.

name.job: The common name of that molecule, e.g. water, methane, ammonia, ethane, methanol.

free-build.job: Ask the student to build any molecule that satisfies one structural constraint, where more than one answer is correct.

constraint.job: The structural property the student's molecule must have. Every atom must still end up with a full valence, and the builder models single bonds only.
